title: Shook Ones hidden piano
hook: Shook Ones hid a Herbie Hancock piano for 16 years.
voiceover: Shook Ones hid a Herbie Hancock piano for 16 years. 1995, Havoc builds Shook Ones Part 2 for The Infamous. That eerie loop, the one that sounds like a kettle about to go, everybody assumed was a keyboard. Nobody could name it. Then around 2011 heads on the sampling forums matched it. It's Herbie Hancock, Jessica, from the 1969 Fat Albert Rotunda album on Warner Bros. Havoc took a couple of seconds of piano, pitched it up hard, and chopped it until the notes stopped sounding like piano. That's why it hid, and Havoc later confirmed it. The lesson for producers, pitch and chop until your own mother wouldn't recognise it. Save this and go hear Jessica.
caption: Shook Ones Part II (Mobb Deep, The Infamous, Loud, 1995, produced by Havoc). For 16 years nobody could name the loop. It's Jessica, from Herbie Hancock's Fat Albert Rotunda (Warner Bros, 1969), pitched up and chopped until the piano stopped sounding like a piano. Identified by sample hunters around 2011, later confirmed by Havoc. What should I break down Monday?
